spec.title: Terminal Context Boundary — Frame's context follows Frame's terminal

tasks.title: Add pure `src/main/launchEnv.js` with `frameBinDir`, idempotent `prependFrameBin` and `supportsWrappers`
tasks.whatChanged: New pure module src/main/launchEnv.js exporting supportsWrappers(platform), frameBinDir(projectPath) and prependFrameBin(pathValue, projectPath, platform). It requires only node:path and frameConstants — no fs, no Electron. Nothing consumes it yet; T09 wires it into the PTY spawn env.
tasks.whyChanged: PATH composition is the one piece of this spec that is pure logic, so it was extracted rather than inlined into pty.js/ptyManager.js, which the testing record says stay untested. supportsWrappers() is the single POSIX gate so no call site does its own process.platform check. prependFrameBin drops any later copy of the bin dir instead of returning early on a match anywhere: a real `claude` earlier on PATH would win and the session would silently lose Frame's context, so the entry must be first, not merely present.

tasks.title: Add `test/launchEnv.test.js` covering idempotent prepending, the platform separator and an untouched PATH off-POSIX
tasks.whatChanged: 12 cases in test/launchEnv.test.js: frameBinDir with and without a project, the POSIX gate, prepend puts the bin dir first, prepending twice is a no-op, an entry sitting behind /usr/local/bin is moved rather than duplicated, the win32 PATH comes back byte-identical, an absent PATH becomes just the bin dir, and empty segments are dropped.
tasks.whyChanged: The purity case does more than grep the source: it reloads the module through a poisoned Module._load that throws on fs/electron and then exercises prependFrameBin, so a require added later fails the test rather than passing a string match. The move-not-duplicate case is the one that would otherwise regress quietly — a present-but-not-first entry still loses to a real CLI earlier on PATH.

tasks.title: Rewrite `getWrapperTemplate` to be recursion-safe and emit its tool's flags
tasks.whatChanged: The wrapper now resolves the real CLI at run time with its own directory filtered out of PATH (`PATH="$(path_without_self)" command -v <tool>`) and execs "$REAL_CLI", so a wrapper named after its tool cannot re-enter itself. It builds a frame_args array from the injection record — promptFlag in front of the preamble or the preamble positionally, settingsFlag appended only when that file exists — and keeps `exec "$REAL_CLI" "$@"` when the preamble is missing. A missing CLI exits 127 with a named message instead of looping.
tasks.whyChanged: Resolution is at run time rather than baked in at write time so a version-manager switch or reinstall is picked up immediately; an absolute path written at project open would go stale silently. The settings flag is conditional on the file existing because the payload is optional while the preamble is not. Deviation from plan.md's sequencing: the three existing wrapper assertions in test/frameTemplates.test.js asserted the old `exec codex ...` shape and were updated here rather than in T04 — a rewrite that leaves the suite red is not a finished task. T04 still adds the four new cases.

verification.detail: 435/435 pass; wrapper also exercised end-to-end in a sandbox — self-exec, arg passthrough, missing preamble, missing settings, absent CLI
